DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 78 s. 2021 JUN 15 2021 MR. JUAN V. GERVASIO Interior F. Manalo, Barangay Malinao, Pasig City Dear Mr. Gervasio: This has reference to your letter seeking assistance on the issue of Idle Lands Tax and illegal settlers in your property in Pasig City. At the outset, taking into account that there are matters that fall squarely under the mandate and technical expertise of Department of Finance — Bureau of Local Government Finance (DoF-BLGF), we deem it proper to defer to their position. In that regard, we shall discuss only the provisions of law or rules which we find applicable based on the representations in the letter. Accordingly, it is noteworthy to highlight that while under Section 236 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code (LGC) of 1991 provide the imposition of an additional ad valorem tax on idle lands, however, Item 6.0 of Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2010-02 issued by this Department with the Department of Finance, provided for the exemption from the levy of such additional ad valorem tax on idle lands, to wit: "Owners of idle lands shall be exempted from payment of the additional levy by reason of force majeure, civil disturbance natural calamity. or any cause or circumstances which h ical or all revent the owners of ro e or person having legal interest therein from improving. utilizinqt or cultivatinq the same. " Consistently, considering that the property was waterlogged due to an abandoned construction coupled with the purported acts of building illegal structures by the alleged informal settlers who encroached on the property lines of the owner, it prevented the owner from further developing, utilizing or cultivating the same. Hence, this Department is of the view that the owner shall be exempted from paying the ad valorem tax on idle land.

Correspondingly, in relation to the alleged informal settlers, this Department would like to emphasize that an owner of a propetty shall have the right to possess, use, enjoy the fruits, dispose or sell, and to recover his/her property. As a result, an owner of a land may file the appropriate case in court in order to obtain possession of such property. Thus, as to the purported acts of building illegal structures which encroaches the owner's property, we are of the iew that these are matters of fact that need to be adjudicated in the proper forum. As to the acts of certain government officials of the city of Pasig, this Department deems it proper to stress that Republic Act No. 11032 (EODB Law), otherwise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Delivery of Government Services Act of 2018", requires all local government units (LGUs) to devise a unified business application form for the issuance of business permits, clearance, and other types of authorizations, as well as set-up a one-stop-shop to facilitate all business transactions. Accordingly, this Department, together with the Department of Trade and Industry and Department of Information and Communication Technology, issued Joint Memorandum Circular (MC) 2016-01 or the Revised Standards in Processing Business Permits and Licenses in All Cities and Municipalities containing the guidelines in streamlining business permits and licensing system. Accordingly, the EODB Law prescribes administrative and criminal liability to the officials and employees who may act inappropriately such as the refusal to accept application or request without due cause. Accordingly, under the Manual on Real Property Appraisal and Assessment Operations, it states that any officer charged with the duty of assessing real property who intentionally violates or fails to perform any duty imposed upon him by law relating to the assessment of taxable real property shall be held liable. This includes any other officer required to perform acts relating to the administration of the real property tax or to assist the assessor or treasurer in such administration, who willfully fails to discharge such duties. Further, under Republic Act No. 6713, otherwise known as the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees", and the Rules Implementing the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, it provides that public officials and employees shall, at all times, be accountable to the people and shall discharge their duties with utmost responsibility, integrity, competence, and loyalty, and uphold public interest over personal interest.

In view of the foregoing, this Department opines that proper administrative proceedings may be instituted or initiated against erring government employees, with the appropriate agency having jurisdiction over such personnel. Thank you. Very truly yours, B the Authority of the Secretary: GAN Underse tary for Local Government LLLS/32 Copy furnished: DIR. MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN Regional Director, DILG-NCR Annex Building, Sugar Center Compound North Ave, Diliman, Quezon City
